name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 98

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: One may be put on for the rest of the continental travellers

definitions.text: One may be put on for the rest of the continental travellers

blocks.clueFragment: One may be put on for the rest
blocks.note: surface reading: something worn or applied so that one can relax, like a nightcap or a face mask
setter's reading: a carriage coupled to a European train so that passengers can sleep on the journey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' means added to a train, not worn, and 'the rest' is a night's sleep. A wagon-lit is the French name for a sleeping car on continental European railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a railway sleeping carriage, attached to continental trains so passengers can sleep on overnight journeys.

clue.text: Girl fastening new belt

indicators.note: a girl fastening something holds it tight within her grasp, so her name wraps around the other letter

blocks.note: a girl's name
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A girl buckles up a brand-new belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a belt in the sense of a band or strip of territory, as in a green belt or a time zone.

clue.text: Holy man found in most suitable robing room

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: as in 'the very thing' or 'the very man for the job', meaning exactly right
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A priest is discovered in the best possible changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most suitable' reads like a superlative such as BEST, but the word wanted is VERY in its adjective sense of precisely right.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where clergy put on their vestments before a service.

clue.text: Braised meat and mashed potato's about right

indicators.note: mashed potato is pulped out of its shape, so the letters of the word are crushed into a new order
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter, apostrophe dropped
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A recipe line: braised meat served alongside mashed potato, more or less correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot roast is a joint of beef or other meat browned and then cooked slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid, which is braising.

clue.text: Means of raising revenue in Texas that changed around end of April?

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters are wrapped about the kept letter

blocks.note: the two words taken letter by letter
the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: A question about a Texan levy introduced around the end of April, the start of the tax year.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is fanciful. A stealth tax is a British term for a levy raised quietly, without voters noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth tax is a charge that brings in money for government without being openly announced as a tax rise.

clue.text: Wretched tailor making for an island in Venice

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, broken state, so the letters of the word are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: An unhappy tailor heads for a Venetian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making for' looks like travel in the surface but is only the link from wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the central island district of Venice, home to the market and the famous bridge over the Grand Canal.

clue.text: Titled lady one's seen in pubs

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: bars are pubs, or the counters in them
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is spotted drinking in local pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding the rank of baron in the peerage, or a baron's wife, so a lady with a title.

clue.text: Famous cricketer becomes serious

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Garfield ..., the great West Indies all-rounder
second meaning: a verb, grows solemn or calms down, as in sobering up

explanation.walkthrough: Garry Sobers is often called the greatest all-rounder in cricket history; the surface makes his name a subject doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the West Indies cricketing legend doubles as the third-person verb for growing grave or sober.

clue.text: Business suit?

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm or organisation
second meaning: a set of clothes worn together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Business suit' reads as one thing, the office wear; split it and each word separately means the answer. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a company or team, informally, and a complete set of clothes, an ensemble.

clue.text: Bay providing shelter, to a large extent

indicators.note: to a large extent means mostly but not wholly, so the word is used minus its final letter

blocks.note: cover is shelter, as in taking cover from rain

explanation.surface: A bay offers ships a good deal of protection from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading the whole clue as a description of a harbour; in fact only 'Bay' defines, and the last letter of COVER is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A cove is a small sheltered bay or inlet on a coast.

clue.text: Place of worship in New Barnet — 50 inside one

indicators.note: new suggests something remade, so the letters of the following word are reworked
inside places one piece within another

blocks.note: the place name taken letter by letter
an ace is a one in cards
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A chapel in New Barnet, a London suburb, with fifty people inside.
explanation.walkthrough: New Barnet is a real district of north London, so 'New' looks like part of the name. It is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a building used for worship, especially a nonconformist chapel, and originally the portable Hebrew sanctuary.

clue.text: Stylish catalogue one female brought out

indicators.note: things brought out are taken away from where they were, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: to catalogue items is to classify them
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A fashion catalogue launches a single elegant woman's range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catalogue' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb; take I and F out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy is an informal adjective for smart, elegant and showing good taste.

clue.text: Feature of a clock, perhaps, that's no longer new

blocks.note: first meaning: the pointer that counts off seconds on a dial
second meaning: previously owned and used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is there because not every clock has this pointer; it marks the first meaning as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun phrase it is the fastest pointer on a watch face; as an adjective it describes used goods bought from a previous owner.

clue.text: Response concerning behaviour

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in the subject line of a letter
one's actions are one's behaviour

explanation.surface: A reply about how someone has been behaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or response to something said or done.

clue.text: A second earthmover tipped over in US port

indicators.note: a load tipped over is upended, so the string of letters is turned back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'
a Cat is a Caterpillar tractor or bulldozer

explanation.surface: A second bulldozer overturns in an American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Caterpillar machines are widely called Cats, which is what 'earthmover' stands for here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacoma is a seaport city in Washington State on Puget Sound.

clue.text: Girl pronounced nickname

indicators.note: pronounced means said out loud, so the answer is spelt as something that is only heard

blocks.note: a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl whose nickname is called out.
explanation.definitionFit: Monicker, also spelt moniker, is informal slang for a name or nickname.

clue.text: Interference in stable

blocks.note: first meaning: crackle on a radio or television signal
second meaning: an adjective, not moving or changing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' wants to be the building for horses, with something interfering inside it; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is noise from atmospheric electricity spoiling reception, and as an adjective means motionless or unchanging.

clue.text: Power tool at home was set up after short discussion

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter
in a down clue, set up means raised the other way, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a chat is an informal talk
someone at home is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A power tool was installed at home after a brief talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the reversed piece behind the other two, which come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a motorised saw with teeth on a driven loop of chain, used for felling and cutting timber.

clue.text: Old wine for sale abroad

blocks.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Vintage wine being offered for sale in another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old wine' reads as one phrase, a vintage; split it into a prefix for former and a type of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made for export are intended for sale in foreign markets, so the word serves as an adjective for overseas trade.

clue.text: A Pope reportedly criticises a religious reformer

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard by word of mouth, so the next piece counts for its sound only

blocks.note: John is a name taken by many popes
to knock something is to criticise it

explanation.surface: A pope is said to attack a Protestant reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox led the Scottish Reformation in the sixteenth century, so the surface of a pope criticising him is historically apt.
explanation.definitionFit: John Knox was the Scottish clergyman who founded Presbyterianism, a leader of the Protestant Reformation.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasant party brought over promissory notes

indicators.note: brought over means turned across to the other side, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A dreadful party guest turns up with a bundle of IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious describes something hateful or repulsive, deeply disagreeable.

clue.text: Steer and first of cows put in rail freight wagon

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
put in means placed inside, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence
a steer is a young castrated bull, a kind of ox
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cattle are loaded into a railway goods wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb about driving, but it is the animal. A boxcar is the American name for an enclosed railway goods van.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxcar is an enclosed railway freight car with sliding doors, chiefly in North America.

clue.text: Swell making one sick in front of ship

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the bow is the forward end of a ship
someone who is sick is ill

explanation.surface: A heavy sea at the bow of a ship makes a passenger seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of ship' wants to select a first letter, S; here it means the bow itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a large sea wave, the same as a swell in its sense of rolling water.

clue.text: Where one may learn peak's chilly, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud by others, so the words count for their sound only

blocks.note: a high is a peak, as in a record high, and chilly means cool

explanation.surface: A mountain-top classroom where the summit is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, the possessive and the adjective run together into the name of a place of education.
explanation.definitionFit: A high school is a secondary school, a place where teenagers study.

clue.text: Stinking row in station

blocks.note: first meaning: smelling foul
second meaning: a line, as of soldiers
third meaning: one's position or standing in society

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions for one word: a smelly row at a train station is the picture, but 'in' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foul-smelling, a line of people or things, and a level in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Runs over to help attack

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for runs in cricket scores
aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone dashes across to lend a hand in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer one piece sits over the next, so 'over' simply places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack or assault, typically a surprise one.

clue.text: One of five given this French fruit

blocks.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: One of five children is handed this piece of French fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, aromatic pear-shaped fruit used in jams and jellies.

clue.text: Very hot current across river

indicators.note: across means spanning from side to side, so this piece stretches either side of the other

blocks.note: current affairs are topical ones
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A scorching flow of water runs over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a flow of water, which suits the river; it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical describes the sweltering heat of the regions near the equator, so it serves for very hot weather.
